{"markdown":"# Issues Memo — EXHIBIT 10.4 (TrueLink Hosting, Support and Interface Agreement)

**To:** Deal team 
**From:** In-house counsel (Client-side) 
**Re:** Playbook review of EXHIBIT 10.4 — verified findings only

---

## 1. Executive summary

We reviewed the Agreement against the playbook and identified **nine deviations or gaps** (three critical, one high, two medium deviations, two medium/low missing clauses) against **twelve compliant positions**. The commercial framework is broadly acceptable to us — there is no exclusivity, non-compete, non-solicit, MFN or audit obligation on Client, Client has an unconditional termination election on roughly a month's notice, renewal is annual with a 30-day opt-out, and TrueLink has granted us a rate MFN — but the risk-allocation articles are materially one-sided.

The four issues that drive the negotiation are: (i) **indemnity asymmetry** — TrueLink offers only a breach-of-contract indemnity with no duty to defend and no IP, breach-of-law, data-breach or wilful-misconduct cover, while Client's indemnity is very broad; (ii) a **one-way limitation of liability** capping TrueLink at 12 months' fees while leaving Client uncapped; (iii) a **worldwide licence for TrueLink to resell and exploit Credit Data** (our borrowers' and applicants' data), coupled with no licence to Client in the results of the Hosting and Support Services; and (iv) **no post-termination transition or data-return mechanic at all**, and **no insurance obligation**, from a vendor that hosts our web site and processes credit data. We have also proposed fallback-level fixes to assignment/change of control, licence scope (affiliates and successors) and the absence of any performance warranty.

Our redlines are deliberately minimal: we retain existing text and cross-references wherever possible and target the fallback position on most items, reserving the preferred position only where the current drafting creates walk-away exposure.

---

## 2. Findings

| # | Severity | Rule | Status | Section | Summary / position taken |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Critical | INDEMN — Indemnification by Vendor | Deviation | § 12 INDEMNITY. | § 12(b) is a breach-of-contract indemnity only (no defence duty, no IP, breach-of-law, data-breach or gross negligence/wilful misconduct cover, no defence procedure); § 12(a) imposes a very broad Client indemnity. Added a TrueLink defence and indemnity with notice/control/cooperation, and narrowed Client's indemnity to Client Content and Client's violations of law. |
| 2 | Critical | IP — Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data | Deviation | § 8 COVENANTS AND WARRANTIES OF CLIENT | § 8(d) lets TrueLink distribute, license, resell and exploit Credit Data independently of service delivery; Client has no licence to the results of the Services. Targeted the fallback: TrueLink keeps its Interface/tools/know-how, Client receives a perpetual deliverables licence, and the Credit Data licence is narrowed to processing to provide the services. |
| 3 | Critical | LOL-CAP — Limitation of liability | Deviation | § 12 INDEMNITY. | Sole cap protects TrueLink alone (12 months' hosting and support compensation); Client's liability is unlimited, including under § 12(a). Carve-outs cover only gross negligence and wilful misconduct. Mutualised the existing 12-month basis and carved out indemnification, confidentiality, gross negligence and wilful misconduct for both parties; scope otherwise untouched. |
| 4 | High | ASSIGN — Assignment and change of control | Deviation | § 12 INDEMNITY. | § 15 requires consent with no successor/M&A carve-out, no notice mechanic and no reasonableness qualifier; no change-of-control trigger anywhere. Qualified consent as not unreasonably withheld, limited the exception to Client affiliate/successor transfers, barred assignment to a TrueLink competitor and confirmed no termination right on a Client change of control. |
| 5 | High | LICENSE — Licence grant scope | Deviation | § 2 LICENSE. | Grant runs to "Client" (Mortgage Logic.com, Inc.) only — no affiliate coverage and, given § 15, no transfer to a successor. Added one short subsection giving affiliate coverage on written notice and a Client-side successor transfer right, without overriding § 15 or expanding TrueLink's assignment rights. |
| 6 | High | EXCLUSIVITY | Compliant | § 2 LICENSE. | No exclusivity or sole-supplier obligation; § 2(a) is non-exclusive and confirms Client may acquire, develop or license competing software and services. Preferred position met. |
| 7 | High | LD — Liquidated damages/penalties on Customer | Compliant | § 5 COMPENSATION. | No liquidated damages, exit fee or accelerated charge payable by Client; § 5 minimums are ongoing service charges and § 14 termination simply runs fees to the last day of the following month. Preferred position met. |
| 8 | High | NONCOMPETE | Compliant | § 2 LICENSE. | No non-compete or field-of-use covenant on Client; § 3(i) sourcing sentence applies only where Client voluntarily uses the Interface. Preferred position met. |
| 9 | High | T4C — Termination for convenience | Compliant | § 12 INDEMNITY. | § 14 gives Client an unconditional termination election on written notice (≈30–60 days) with no early-termination fee; TrueLink has no mid-term convenience right. At or above fallback. |
| 10 | Medium | MINCOMMIT — Minimum commitments | Compliant (fallback) | § 5 COMPENSATION. | § 5(a) imposes a monthly minimum, so the preferred position is not met, but it sits at the fallback: one-year term with 30 days' non-renewal notice, unconditional Client exit on ≈a month's notice, and no shortfall penalty or accelerated minimum. |
| 11 | Medium | GOVLAW — Governing law and venue | Compliant (fallback) | § 12 INDEMNITY. | §§ 26–27 select California law and exclusive courts in San Luis Obispo County; no arbitration. Sits at the fallback; New York preference and the Vendor-convenient county are noted only. |
| 12 | Medium | RENEWAL — Auto-renewal and notice window | Compliant | § 12 INDEMNITY. | § 13: successive one-year renewals with a 30-day mutual non-renewal notice; no renewal uplift mechanic. At the preferred 30-day opt-out level; absence of a Vendor reminder noted only. |
| 13 | Medium | AUDIT — Audit rights against Customer | Compliant | § 5 COMPENSATION. | No audit, inspection or usage-verification right binding Client; §§ 5–6 run in our favour. Better than preferred; nothing to redline. |
| 14 | Medium | MFN | Compliant | § 5 COMPENSATION. | The only MFN runs in our favour (§ 6 rate commitment plus one-year price freeze); no MFN burdens Client. Preferred position met. |
| 15 | Medium | NOSOLICIT | Compliant | § 8 COVENANTS AND WARRANTIES OF CLIENT | No non-solicitation, no-hire or anti-poaching covenant on Client anywhere. Preferred position met. |
| 16 | Medium | WARRANTY — Performance warranty | Deviation | § 8 COVENANTS AND WARRANTIES OF CLIENT | Only warranty is the § 9 Y2K date-processing warranty; § 3 service levels are "reasonable commercial efforts" only and there is no conformance warranty or remedy. Inserted the fallback: 90 days' software conformance to documentation, 30 days for the Services, with repair, replacement or refund. |
| 17 | Medium | TRANSITION — Transition assistance and data return | Missing | § 12 INDEMNITY. | §§ 13–14 contain no transition assistance, data export/return or deletion mechanic (and place migration burdens on us); § 10 has no return-or-destroy obligation. Inserted six months' assistance at then-current rates, machine-readable return within 30 days, and certified deletion after return. |
| 18 | Low | INSURANCE — Vendor insurance | Missing | § 12 INDEMNITY. | No insurance obligation anywhere, despite TrueLink hosting our web site and processing Client Content and Credit Data. Inserted a short fallback clause (E&O USD 1M; cyber/privacy USD 2M) after § 30. |

---

## 3. Walk-away items

The following are identified in the findings as walk-away or near walk-away territory and should not be conceded without escalation:

1. **One-way limitation of liability (§ 12, LOL-CAP).** A cap protecting only the Vendor while Client's liability — including under the broad § 12(a) indemnity — is unlimited. We require mutuality plus carve-outs for indemnification, confidentiality, gross negligence and wilful misconduct.
2. **Indemnity package (§ 12, INDEMN).** No Vendor IP indemnity anywhere in the document, no duty to defend and no defence procedure, against a very broad Client indemnity. This fails the fallback and approaches walk-away.
3. **No data return on termination (TRANSITION).** The complete absence of any data export, return or deletion obligation is walk-away territory; the inserted clause is at the preferred level for that reason.
4. **No insurance (INSURANCE).** For a vendor handling personal and credit data, the absence of any coverage obligation is walk-away territory; we have proposed only fallback limits.

We would also treat the § 8(d) Credit Data exploitation licence as a red-line item on substance: TrueLink reselling our borrowers' and applicants' data is outside anything the services require.

---

## 4. Next steps

1. **Issue the redline** covering the six drafted proposals: mutual liability cap with carve-outs (§ 12), TrueLink indemnity plus narrowed Client indemnity (§ 12), deliverables licence and narrowed Credit Data licence (§§ 2/8), assignment and change of control (§ 15), licence scope for affiliates and successors (§ 2), performance warranty (§ 9 area), transition and data return (after § 14) and insurance (after § 30).
2. **Lead the negotiation on the four walk-away items**; treat warranty, assignment, licence scope and insurance as fallback-level trades available in exchange.
3. **Confirm we are not re-trading compliant terms.** No changes are sought to exclusivity, non-compete, non-solicit, MFN, audit, liquidated damages, termination for convenience, renewal, governing law or the minimum commitment structure; all sit at the preferred position or acceptably at the fallback.
4. **Diligence request:** obtain and review the separate **Non-Competition Agreement** referenced in § 8(d) — it is outside this document and was not reviewed; check in particular for any personnel covenants against the non-solicitation fallback.
5. **Housekeeping for the next turn:** tidy the loose cross-references noted under MINCOMMIT (§ 14's "Subject to Section 4" and § 6's reference to "minimum monthly fees listed in Section 4", where the minimums appear in § 5), and § 6's bar on contesting or obtaining backup for the minimum fees.
6. **Optional asks if the negotiation remains open:** LOL-CAP preferred items (USD 1,000,000 floor, "paid or payable", mutual consequential-damages waiver, data protection/security, fraud and IP carve-outs), a renewal reminder 60 days before each term, an express pro-rata refund on termination, and a New York law/venue or at least a less Vendor-convenient California county.
"}
